caption:
A medical mistake took her sight as an infant. She spent her life giving 200 other blind people their independence back.

Tiffany Brar was born in Chennai and lost her sight as an infant due to oxygen toxicity (Terry Syndrome) - a medical accident, not a condition she was born with. She studied at the Mary Scott Home for the Blind in Darjeeling before starting the Jyothirgamaya mobile school for the blind in 2012, which grew into a nonprofit foundation teaching life skills to blind people of all ages across rural Kerala. She has trained over 200 blind people in Braille, computer skills and other life skills. In 2022 - still her most recent major honor - the President of India awarded her the Nari Shakti Puraskar, the country's highest civilian honor for women, for empowering visually impaired rural women.
